variants.headline: {{aggressor}} marches on {{ally}}
body: {{aggressor}} has opened war against {{ally}}, a small power allied to us. In the ally's market, the shutters went up before the first soldiers were seen. Our soldiers are not in the fighting.

variants.headline: One of our small allies is at war
body: War has come to one of the small powers allied to us. A carter on that road has turned back twice; the dispatches name the fighting but not every banner in it.

variants.headline: Why the attack on {{ally}} matters
body: The attack on {{ally}} is a test of more than one small state's walls. {{aggressor}} has shown where its armies point, and an army that points once will point twice. The council should be counting what it costs to back an ally, before the bill arrives with the next war.

variants.headline: {{aggressor}} opens war on {{ally}}
body: Notice to carriers: {{aggressor}} has opened hostilities against {{ally}}, a small power in alliance with this nation. Those bound for its market should look for another road. Our own peace stands unbroken.

variants.headline: An ally is at war. What is our answer?
body: Citizens, war has been declared on {{ally}}. Our council should tell the ally what it can send, and when; a town that needs grain and timber for its defenses has no use for a promise that comes after the roads close.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} falls to {{captor}}
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}} by conquest. A trader who kept a stall inside its gate has brought his goods home; the small power that was our ally now answers to a foreign flag.

variants.headline: An allied city-state is taken
body: A small power allied to us has fallen to a foreign army. The dispatches before us do not carry every name, but the list of our allies is one shorter.

variants.headline: What we lost with {{cityState}}
body: The flag of {{captor}} now flies over {{cityState}}. A carter who used to change horses there is looking for a stop outside town; if enough drivers do the same, the city's stable keepers could lose the trade they once counted on.

variants.headline: {{cityState}}, faithful to the last
body: {{cityState}} kept its own council among the small powers, and it gave its alliance to our nation, and it kept both until the end. The swords came, and the city fell, and the name passes into the record: a province under another hand, an alliance kept to the last.

variants.headline: Tell our allies when help can reach them
body: Our ally {{cityState}} has fallen to {{captor}}. Before the next city counts on our protection, the council should tell it what help we can send and how fast. A town that knows when to expect us can decide whether it can afford to hold out.

variants.when: cityState !== null && captor !== null && distance !== null
variants.headline: Our ally falls {{distance}} tiles from home
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}}, {{distance}} tiles from our nearest town. One carter has cousins there. He's been asking everyone coming down the road for word of them.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} defects to {{rival}}
body: {{cityState}}, a small power near our borders, has ended its alliance with us and named {{rival}} in its place. The envoy who kept our friendship there is packing his ledgers for the road home.

variants.headline: A neighbor's friendship changes hands
body: One of the small powers near us has given its alliance to a rival power. Our own arrangement with it has ended, and the envoys who kept it are coming home.

variants.headline: Would more gold have kept {{cityState}}?
body: {{cityState}} has switched its alliance from us to {{rival}}. The capital may suspect it was outbid. If the city was looking for help with a border quarrel, though, even a larger gift from us could go down as a courtesy and leave the alliance where it is.

variants.headline: The flags came down at {{cityState}}
body: Our colors flew over {{cityState}}'s gate for years, or so the caravans told it. This week the watch changed, and {{rival}}'s emblem went up in their place. The gate did not move; everything else did.

variants.headline: A letter from the frontier
body: Madam Editor: I keep a stall where the road meets {{cityState}}'s market, and I have watched the envoys come and go. Lately more of them wore {{rival}}'s colors. When the alliance changed this week, no one on my road was surprised.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} names us its ally
body: {{cityState}} has named this nation its ally, ending whatever arrangement it had before. Its envoy asked, before he sat down, what we mean to send and when.

variants.headline: A small power chooses us
body: One of the small powers has ended its former arrangement and named this nation its ally. The friendship is ours now, and so is the work of keeping it.

variants.headline: What {{cityState}} opens to us
body: We have a new ally in {{cityState}}, {{distance}} tiles away on the survey map. The traders here are already asking their guild which goods might sell there. Our envoys have a chance to make introductions while both sides still remember the ceremony.

variants.headline: Notice: our envoys succeed in {{cityState}}
body: Notice is given that {{cityState}} has ended its alliance with {{replaced}} and named this nation in its place. The government's envoys, backed with patience and coin, are owed the credit. Traders bound for its market should call at the foreign office for a letter of introduction.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{cityState}} stands with us
body: Hear it, people of the court and the road! {{cityState}} has named this nation its ally! Its friendship stands with our flag! {{cityState}} stands with us! Let the news carry to every gate!

variants.headline: {{cityState}} walks away from our alliance
body: Our alliance with {{cityState}} has ended, and no other power has taken our place. In the capital, the keeper of the book of friendships has struck out the city's name.

variants.headline: Our ally leaves, and no one follows
body: One of the small powers has ended its alliance with us. No other nation has been named in its place; the seat beside it stands empty, and empty seats do not stay empty for long.

variants.headline: Who lost {{cityState}}?
body: Alliances do not end in a day; they leak. {{cityState}} has walked away from us without walking toward anyone, and that is the part that should worry the capital. A rival did not buy this ally. We misplaced it.

variants.headline: The alliance with {{cityState}} ends
body: In this season the alliance between our nation and {{cityState}} came to its end. No ally was named in our place. The city-state remains in the record of the powers, its friendship ungiven.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} account, closed
body: Alliance with this nation: ended.
Named in our place: no one.
Balance remaining: one small power, free to choose, and choosing nothing.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} switches its alliance to {{friend}}
body: {{cityState}} has named {{friend}} its ally, ending the alliance it held with us. Our envoy hands his letters to {{friend}}'s man in the square. {{friend}} is a declared friend, so the alliance leaves our hands, but not into an enemy's.

variants.headline: An ally passes to a friend
body: A small power near us has ended its alliance with this nation and given it to a power we count as a friend. It is a loss, and the gentlest kind of one.

variants.headline: A go-between for {{cityState}}
body: {{cityState}} has chosen {{friend}} in our place. If a dispute over a road or a field comes up now, both sides still have someone they can talk to. {{friend}} can sound out the two towns before the quarrel grows serious enough to call for a formal protest.

variants.headline: Notice of a new ally in {{cityState}}
body: It is noted for the record that {{cityState}}, a {{distance}}-day journey from our nearest city, has named {{friend}} its ally. Our own alliance with the city-state ends with the season, and it ends among friends.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} changes allies tonight
body: From the small powers tonight: {{cityState}} has a new ally, {{friend}}. The city-state sits {{distance}} days from our border. Our own alliance with it has ended. The new ally is a declared friend of this nation.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} counts us a friend
body: Our standing with {{cityState}} has risen into friendship, short of alliance. The city-state's gates and its council are now open to us as they are to any friend.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} is friendly no longer
body: Our standing with {{cityState}} has fallen out of friendship. The welcome at its gates is thinner now, and the conversation at its council shorter.

variants.headline: Friendship recorded with {{cityState}}
body: Be it recorded that friendship now holds between this nation and {{cityState}}, from the present season. The scribes of the small power have entered it in their book, and our own in ours.

variants.headline: We let a friendship lapse
body: Friendship with {{cityState}} is over, and no rival took it from us. Regard like that is kept by attention, and ours stopped arriving seasons ago. The envoys owe the capital an explanation for how a neighbor's regard was left to cool.

variants.headline: A word at the fire
body: They say at the fire: the guest who forgets the house is forgotten by the door. So stands our friendship with {{cityState}}.

variants.headline: A deadline comes off {{cityState}}'s board
body: A deadline has come off the board at {{cityState}}. A traveler who had already put money aside for the trip says she will keep it another week before she spends it on something else.

variants.headline: A small power's notice board loses a deadline
body: A deadline has come off a small power's notice board this week, and the mason who had priced stone for the job is asking whether the order still stands.

variants.headline: Notice: an errand ends in {{cityState}}
body: For the information of merchants and travelers: {{cityState}} has taken one of its posted errands off the board, deadline and all. Those who priced work for it should ask at the gate before they spend more on the road.

variants.headline: The missing date on {{cityState}}'s board
body: The errand board in {{cityState}} no longer lists the job that was due at {{previousDeadline}}. One man who had been saving his good boots for the trip says he will wait to hear whether the work still stands.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} deadline is {{turnsLeft}} days out
body: {{cityState}} has an errand on its board whose deadline falls in {{turnsLeft}} days. A hauler has taken the last of the goods aboard and means to reach the city before it closes.

variants.headline: A {{cityState}} errand ends today
body: The deadline {{cityState}} posted for its errand falls today. When the sun sets on it, the work is done or it is not.

variants.headline: A small power's errand is nearly due
body: An errand posted by a city-state is nearly due. A traveler who means to answer it says he has asked the next cart leaving town to take him as far as it can.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} clock hits zero
body: The {{cityState}} errand closes today. Done is done. Not done is not getting done.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{turnsLeft}} days on the {{cityState}} errand
body: Hear it, all with a stake in the {{cityState}} errand! {{turnsLeft}} days remain, and the sand runs fast! {{turnsLeft}} days! The errand will not wait, and neither should you!

variants.headline: {{cityState}} posts an errand with a deadline
body: A new errand has gone up on {{cityState}}'s board, with {{turnsLeft}} days allowed for the doing. A tanner read it twice, then went to find his partner; the work would need both.

variants.headline: A new errand, and a deadline
body: One of the small powers has posted a new errand with {{turnsLeft}} days on it. The first of those days is already gone.

variants.headline: New errand posted in {{cityState}}
body: From the notices tonight: {{cityState}} has posted a new errand. The deadline: {{turnsLeft}} days. The days are already running.

variants.headline: A clock worth beating
body: {{cityState}} has posted an errand with {{turnsLeft}} days on it, room enough for serious work. A prize with a schedule attached is still a prize, and it goes to whoever moves first. The realm should be moving.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} wins the alliance of {{cityState}}
body: The small power {{cityState}} has taken {{civilization}} as its ally. At its gate, the watch raised {{civilization}}'s colors, a {{distance}}-day journey from our nearest city.

variants.headline: A great power gains a small friend
body: A small power near our borders has given its alliance to a foreign power, one of the great ones. The new arrangement stands a {{distance}}-day journey from our nearest city.

variants.headline: A foothold {{distance}} days from our walls
body: {{civilization}} now holds the friendship of {{cityState}}, whose ground lies {{distance}} days from our nearest city. Such friendship is bought with gold and patience and spent like ground: another flag where ours might have flown. A power that collects friends this close to our walls is not collecting them for nothing.

variants.headline: Citizens! {{civilization}} wins a neighbor
body: Citizens, {{civilization}} now has an ally in nearby {{cityState}}. The carters at our end are asking whose men they'll meet when they bring in the wool. Our court owes them an answer before they're left to find out at the gate.

variants.when: cityState !== null && civilization !== null && replaced !== null
variants.headline: The seat is still warm
body: {{cityState}} has a new ally: {{civilization}}, who will now enjoy everything {{replaced}} enjoyed about the arrangement.

variants.headline: {{aggressor}} makes war on our friend {{cityState}}
body: {{aggressor}} has opened war on {{cityState}}, a small power joined to this nation by declared friendship. Its traders have pulled their goods off the road, and the fighting is not ours.

variants.headline: A friendly city-state under attack
body: War has reached one of the small powers that call us friend. On the road from its market, a wool trader is asking every driver whether the way is still open.

variants.headline: What the war on {{cityState}} reveals
body: Watch what {{aggressor}} did to {{cityState}}, because it tells you what {{aggressor}} is. A power that will march over a friendly small state has told you how it weighs friendship. We are not in this war. We are simply standing where the lesson is visible.

variants.headline: It is told that war came to {{cityState}}
body: The roads say it, and the roads all say the same: {{aggressor}} has made war on {{cityState}}, the small state that calls us friend. Our sons are not in that fighting. For that, every hearth gives thanks.

variants.headline: War reaches {{cityState}}
body: Notice to traders: {{aggressor}} has opened hostilities against {{cityState}}, a small power that counts us friend. Those bound for its market should take another road. The war has not asked for our arms, and the government has offered none.

variants.headline: Our friend {{cityState}} falls to {{captor}}
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}} by conquest. The small power counted this nation a friend, and its ground now lies under a foreign flag.

variants.headline: A friendly city-state is taken
body: A small power in friendship with this nation has fallen to a foreign army. Our reports lack some of the names; the empty place at our side does not.

variants.headline: The passing of {{cityState}}
body: In the record of the small powers, {{cityState}} held its place among the friendliest. It kept our friendship to the end and lost its independence by the sword. Its altars stand under another hand now; may they be allowed to burn.

variants.headline: Conquest near our borders
body: Tonight, {{captor}} holds a friendly city-state. The conquest is complete. The fighting took place {{distance}} days from our nearest city. That is close. Watch this border.

variants.headline: Letters from the frontier: {{cityState}} is taken
body: Letters from the frontier relate that {{captor}} has completed the conquest of {{cityState}}, a small power in friendship with this nation. The place passes out of the list of independent powers, and this paper sends condolence where it may.
